surprises: ev_context_003 Minkiewicz sentiment was corrected from negative to mixed. The negative judges only his latest programme ('program zrobil slaby'), while the earlier one is praised ('poprzednie mial duzo lepsze'). The schema has no programme-scope field, so programme-scoped evaluations can be read as performer-level sentiment. The v2 prompt should say how to label them.

Minkiewicz-Pacześ style relation conflicts across fans: ev_context_002 calls Minkiewicz 'trochę przeciwieństwem' (a bit of the opposite) of Pacześ; ev_context_003 says he 'chciał być jak Paczes' (wanted to be like him). Both are kept as individual readings and neither supports a similarity or dissimilarity edge. Not adjudicated.

assumptions: The supplied candidate excerpts are the complete author posts, as the collector reports. This was not checked against the live page.
Mention entries are one per performer per record. Extra in-text occurrences are noted but not added.
Under v2, a performer named only as a comparison anchor is neutral, and the comparison does not imply a like or dislike.
A programme-scoped negative whose text also praises an earlier programme is labelled mixed at performer level. This is a judgment call.
Surname-only resolution (Giza) is valid because the performer universe has no competing Giza.
Lowering Minkiewicz's mention confidence from 0.98 to 0.85 is a reviewer judgment, not a measured value.
limitations: No live fetch or new evidence search, so excerpt completeness and verbatim accuracy against standup.pl/gry-online are unverified.
The validator checks schema and performer-ID membership only. It does not check sentiment semantics or record review quality.
Only three records were reviewed. The mention-occurrence policy and programme-scoping rule need a decision before the batch run.
No graph edges were created; the evidence-class decisions are inputs for later stages only.
